correctness.rationale: Writing each Bernoulli modal mass as \(u=(1+r)^{-1}\) and \(v=(1+s)^{-1}\) with \(r,s\in[0,1]\) reduces the convolution to exactly two orientation patterns. In the aligned pattern the normalized maximum is \(c=\max\{1,r+s\}\); in the opposed pattern it is \(c=1+rs\). In both cases \(c\le1+r\) and \(c\le1+s\), which is exactly equivalent to the claimed coefficient \(1/2\). Equality analysis covers deterministic boundaries and shows that the only positive-deficit equality case is the fair pair. No finite computation is used to prove a universal statement.

value.rationale: The supporting source leaves a large gap between known lower constants and the sharp universal upper obstruction \(1/2\), with that obstruction already witnessed by two fair Bernoulli variables. Establishing that \(1/2\) is the exact constant for the entire heterogeneous two-Bernoulli class is a natural finite-summand benchmark: it proves the upper witness is not an isolated example and shows that any Bernoulli-sum obstruction below \(1/2\) must first appear with at least three summands. The equality classification is exact and structural rather than a numerical slice.
